If everything looks good to you, select "Start."

advanced.title: Advanced settings
advanced.warning: Do not touch unless you know what you're doing!
advanced.group_policy_unavailable: Group Policy changes are available only on supported non-Home Windows editions. Talon must be able to identify your edition.
advanced.program_packages_required: Add packages with Program Packages before enabling this step.
advanced.group_policy_changes_required: Add changes with Group Policy Changes before enabling this step.
advanced.internet_required: An internet connection is required for installation.
advanced.browser_required: Select a browser before enabling this step.

dialogs.program_packages_help: Enter one Chocolatey package ID per line, for example: 7zip, vlc, or notepadplusplus (each on its own line). Enter IDs only, without commands or options. Saving does not enable installation: set Install programs through Chocolatey to true in Advanced settings. Clearing this list disables that step.
dialogs.group_policy_changes_help: Enter a JSON array of registry-based Local Group Policy changes. Each object needs hive (HKLM for Computer Configuration or HKCU for User Configuration), key_path, name, value_type (REG_DWORD or REG_SZ), and value (an integer or string respectively). User Configuration applies to users of this computer. Use keys under Software\Policies or Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies; escape backslashes as \\ in JSON. Saving does not enable changes: set Apply Local Group Policy changes to true in Advanced settings. An empty array disables that step.

remove_edge.tooltip: Removes the stable Microsoft Edge browser while preserving browser profiles, WebView2, and other Edge channels. Applies an Edge-specific installation policy on domain-joined systems. Windows or another installer may restore Edge later.

uninstall_outlook_onedrive.tooltip: Uninstalls the Outlook app and OneDrive, as many people do not use them. You can always reinstall them yourself if you want.

program_installation.tooltip: Installs the Chocolatey packages listed in Advanced settings. This step is off by default and requires internet access.

group_policy.tooltip: Applies the registry-based Local Group Policy changes listed in Advanced settings. This step is off by default and is available only on supported non-Home Windows editions.

debloat_windows_phase_one.tooltip: Talon uses a popular and well-established tool, WinUtil by ChrisTitusTech, as part of its debloating process. The whole process is automated, so you don't need to do anything. It is not recommended to remove this step.

debloat_windows_phase_two.tooltip: Talon uses a popular and well-established tool, Win11Debloat by Raphire, as part of its debloating process. The whole process is automated, so you don't need to do anything. It is not recommended to remove this step.

registry_tweaks.tooltip: Modifies the Windows Registry to make your desktop look and feel better, including but not limited to changing your taskbar to be left-aligned, setting your theme to dark theme, removing delay in menus, and showing file extensions.

configure_updates.tooltip: On Pro, Education, and Enterprise editions, uses Windows Update for Business policies to defer feature updates for up to 365 days after release and quality updates (including security fixes) for 4 days, exclude drivers, and notify before downloading updates. On Home, uses registry settings to target the currently installed Windows 11 release and request a 4-day quality-update delay. Home does not have official Windows Update for Business support. Updates are not disabled or restricted to security fixes.

apply_background.tooltip: To complete the look of a freshly debloated system, Talon sets your desktop background to a custom Raven-branded one. The exact desktop background of choice is configurable in the Advanced settings.

developer_mode.tooltip: When enabled, Talon runs without showing the full-screen install overlay.

edge.tooltip: Edge is not recommended unless necessary for your purposes, as it is very invasive to your privacy and embeds ads.

waterfox.tooltip: Waterfox is recommended over Firefox, but not Brave. It's based on Firefox, but removes tracking and telemetry.

brave.tooltip: Brave is the recommended browser, as it is the closest to Chrome while respecting your privacy.

librewolf.tooltip: LibreWolf is only recommended for tech-savvy users. It is designed for maximum privacy and security, but can be harder to use.

firefox.tooltip: Firefox is not recommended unless necessary for your purposes, as it includes telemetry and sponsored content by default.
